eyebrow: The gap every earlier chapter assumed away
code:
ServiceNow's cloud                 Customer's own network
+----------------+                 +---------------------------+
|  SN instance   |                 |  firewall                 |
|  (public URL)  |      ???        |  internal DB, legacy app, |
+----------------+                 |  network device, monitor  |
                                    +---------------------------+

No public endpoint behind the firewall = nothing for the
cloud instance to call directly.
caption: Chapters 2-6 assumed a reachable endpoint on both ends. Internal systems have none.

eyebrow: A MID Server closes the gap
code:
ServiceNow's cloud                 Customer's own network
+----------------+                 +---------------------------+
|  SN instance   | <== outbound == |  MID Server (Java)        |
|                |     polling     |  installed on customer    |
+----------------+                 |  infrastructure           |
                                    |       |                   |
                                    |  internal DB, legacy app, |
                                    |  network device, monitor  |
                                    +---------------------------+
caption: The MID Server reaches outward, from inside the firewall, to poll for work.

steps.label: Real installed software
steps.sub: a Java application the customer runs on their own machine, not a ServiceNow-hosted service

steps.label: Outbound-only
steps.sub: the MID Server always calls out to the instance and polls; the instance never connects inward

steps.label: No inbound port
steps.sub: the customer's firewall stays fully closed to inbound traffic — the default every security team wants
